title: Team
text:
Hi there! I’m Michela.



Photo of Michela petting a cow in the Swiss Alps


I’m a quantitative ecologist with a particular interest for sexual selection. I aim to answer questions related to the evolution of sexual dimorphism in the wild using long-term individual-based datasets. I’m also broadly interested in the effects of climate change and direct human impacts on wild populations.
Currently, I am Wildlife Research Analyst with the Ontario Public Service (Ministry of Natural Resources). My work contributes to monitoring caribou populations in Ontario for the purpose of management and policy decision-making
Previously, I worked as a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at the University of Ottawa, where I built on work I undertook during my PhD under the supervision of Prof. Julien Martin (M.A.D. Lab, University of Ottawa, Canada) and Dr. Pierre Bize (Bize Lab, Swiss Ornithological Institute - Vogelwarte Sempach, Switzerland).
For more information on my work, check out my projects.
I spend most of my free time backpacking or otherwise enjoying the great outdoors. You’ll find a smattering of photos from some of my favourite adventures throughout this website!

Education
 Ph.D. in Biology University of Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. 2020-2024.
 M.Sc. in Ethology Université Paris Sorbonne Nord, Ile-de-France, France. 2018-2020.
 B.Sc. in Biology Honours, with speciallization in Ecology, Ecolution, and Behaviour, with a minor in Psychology. 2012-2017.

title: Dumas Lab - Evolutionary Ecology in the Wild
text:
Evolutionary Ecology · Sexual Dimorphism · Long-term Data · Individual Variation · Environmental Change

Welcome!
The Dumas Lab is based at Laurentian University, in the School of Natural Sciences. We seek to better understand how wild populations respond to changing environments, with a particular focus on sex-specific differences. We use quantitative genetics, genomics, and long-term ecological datasets to investigate the importance of evolutionary processes in shaping current trends and to make predictions about species persistence in Northern Ontario and beyond.
Our research broadly seeks to answer the question: How do animals respond to changing environments, and how do evolutionary processes shape the future of wild populations?


Research Themes




Evolutionary Ecology
How do natural and sexual selection shape variation and evolutionary change in wild populations?





Sex-specific Evolution
Why do males and females differ, and how do evolutionary processes act differently between the sexes?





Quantitative Genetics
How do genes and environmental conditions contribute to individual differences and evolutionary potential?





Wildlife in a Changing World
How do climate change and human-driven environmental disturbance influence wildlife populations?





An Inclusive Research Environment
We believe that excellent science benefits from diverse perspectives, experiences, and ways of thinking. We are committed to fostering a welcoming, respectful, and inclusive research environment where everyone feels valued, supported, and able to contribute.
We strive to provide equitable opportunities for learning, mentorship, and professional development, and to create a lab culture where curiosity, collaboration, and mutual respect are central.


Explore the Lab
Interested in our research, looking for a research opportunity, or curious about joining the team? Explore our projects, meet the people behind the science, and get in touch!

title: Dumas Lab Website — Publishing Workflow
text:
This website uses Quarto + Babelquarto for bilingual rendering and GitHub Pages (gh-pages) for deployment.



main: Website source files (.qmd, _quarto.yml, CSS, images, etc.) and rendered output in docs/.
gh-pages: Published website (rendered HTML files and assets at the branch root).
GitHub Pages deploys from gh-pages → /(root).

Important: Always develop on main. Never manually edit the gh-pages branch.




After editing the website, open the R console and run:
babelquarto::render_website()
This renders both English and French versions into docs/.
Check the preview to make sure both languages look correct.



In the VS Code terminal, make sure you are on main:
git branch
The active branch should have an asterisk (*) beside main.
Then stage, commit, and push your changes:
git add .
git commit -m "Describe website updates"
git push origin main
Replace "Describe website updates" with a short description of your changes.
If there are no new changes to commit, skip the commit step.



Still on main, run:
quarto publish gh-pages --no-render
The --no-render flag is important because Babelquarto has already rendered both language versions. This prevents Quarto from performing a separate render before publishing.
If prompted, confirm the GitHub Pages publishing destination.



Visit:
https://micheladumas.github.io/
Allow a little time for GitHub Pages to deploy the changes. Refresh the page if necessary.




Every time you update the website:

Edit source files on main.
Render both languages:
babelquarto::render_website()
Commit and push source files:
git add .
git commit -m "Update website"
git push origin main
Publish the rendered website:
quarto publish gh-pages --no-render
Check the live website:
https://micheladumas.github.io/








Command
What it does




git status
Check for uncommitted changes


git branch
See your branches and current branch


git switch main
Switch to the source branch


git pull origin main
Pull the latest source changes


git log --oneline -5
View the five most recent commits


git remote -v
Check your GitHub remote



Golden rule: Work on main, render with Babelquarto, publish with Quarto. No manual copying, no subtree commands, and no need to switch branches to deploy!

title: Teaching
text:
Bellow is a short description of the courses I am teaching at Laurentian University. For more details about course content, consult the university webpage, or feel free to reach out!

BIOL-2356FL - Principes d’écologies
Ce cours traite des écosystèmes, des cycles biogéochimiques, de l’énergie écologique, de l’organisation et de la dynamique des communautés biotiques, du rapport entre l’écologie et l’être humain, de la chaîne alimentaire, de la démographie et de l’épidémiologie.
Course to be taught in French. Fall 2027.


BIOL-2706EL - Vertebrate Form and Function
This course is a comparative examination of the important features of the structure and functioning of the chordates with emphasis on the vertebrates and their evolutionary relationships. Course includes laboratory study of the anatomy of selected vertebrates.
Course to be taught in English. Winter 2028


BIOL-3327EL - Experimental Methods in Biology
This course examines the nature of scientific inquiry; biological philosophy and classic biological experiments; the modern research problem; experimental design and analysis; interpretation of results; and presentation of results for publication. It involves searches in scientific journals and abstracts. Students must have knowledge of basic statistical methods.
Course to be taught in English. Winter 2028
